answer: A volcano erupts when hot magma from deep underground rises through a vent, and gas pushes it out as lava, ash and steam.
title: How a volcano erupts
layout: a volcano cross section in the middle on the ground line at y 242; the magma chamber deep below the vent; lava flowing down the right slope; the ash cloud and gas rising above the crater
intro: Let's look at the inside of a volcano to see how it erupts.
summary: Magma gathers in the chamber, rises through the vent, and erupts as lava, gas and ash.

parts.label: Volcano cone
parts.say: The cone is built up from layers of hardened lava and ash.

parts.label: Vent and crater
parts.say: The vent is a pipe that carries magma up to the crater at the top.

parts.label: Magma chamber
parts.say: Deep underground, a pool of hot melted rock called magma builds up.

parts.label: Lava flow
parts.say: Melted rock pours out of the crater and runs down the slope as lava.

parts.label: Ash cloud
parts.say: Tiny bits of ash are blown high into the sky and spread out like a cloud.

parts.label: Gas and steam
parts.say: Gases like steam push upward and help force the magma out of the vent.
